title: SYSK Selects: The Star Wars Holiday Special of 1978
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the episode on the 1978 Star Wars Holiday Special, released as a holiday tradition. The hosts cover Life Day, the Wookiee-centered plot set on Kashyyyk, and how George Lucas gave CBS a variety-show-style special that was made in a hurry. They discuss the writers and producers (Bruce Vilanch, Lenny Rips, the Welch couple, David Acomba and replacement director Steve Binder), the cast (Harvey Korman, Art Carney, Bea Arthur, Diahann Carroll, Jefferson Starship, Carrie Fisher's song), the 1978 CBS broadcast and ratings, the cartoon that introduced Boba Fett, the Vanity Fair and A.V. Club reviews, the disputed sledgehammer quote, and the special's later availability. Closes with listener mail about the Voynich Manuscript podcast.

topics: Star Wars Christmas special Lucas sledgehammer quote

segments.title: Opening banter and Life Day introduction
segments.summary: The hosts kick off the rerun, note the annual holiday tradition, and explain Life Day, the Wookiee celebration held every three years. They describe the special as one of the worst things ever aired and say it is worth watching.

segments.title: Star Wars mania and the origin of the special
segments.summary: The hosts describe the success of Star Wars and how George Lucas, wanting to keep the franchise in front of audiences, was approached by CBS executives about a TV special. Lucas agreed to a Wookiee-focused story set on Kashyyyk, reportedly because the planet had been left out of the films.

segments.title: Variety show format and the production team
segments.summary: The special was built as a variety show because of its TV-special tradition, though variety shows were fading. Writers and producers including Bruce Vilanch, Lenny Rips, and the Welch couple were hired, and David Acomba directed initially before leaving. Shields and Yarnell writers were also brought in.

segments.title: Cast reluctance and the Wookiee dialogue
segments.summary: Harrison Ford, Mark Hamill, and Carrie Fisher had little leverage and appear reluctant. The writers left Wookiee dialogue unsubtitled, and about ten minutes of it plays early on. Vilanch recounts a clash with Lucas over the approach.

segments.title: Broadcast, ratings, and the plot
segments.summary: The special aired November 17, 1978 and drew about thirteen million viewers in the second hour. It was originally planned as an hour but was extended to two because of advertiser interest. The plot follows Han Solo and Chewbacca trying to reach Kashyyyk for Life Day while the family waits.

segments.title: Guest stars and sketches
segments.summary: The hosts describe Harvey Korman's roles, including a Julia Child-style cooking segment, Art Carney as a trader, Bea Arthur at the cantina, and Diahann Carroll in a risque hologram sequence. They also describe the Jefferson Starship music video played on a hologram.

segments.title: Boba Fett cartoon, ending, and aftermath
segments.summary: A cartoon that introduces Boba Fett is discussed as the high point of the special. The ending has a stormtrooper die after tripping, followed by a Life Day celebration and Carrie Fisher's song. The hosts recount Lucas's later comments and his claim that he didn't sledgehammer copies, the Carrie Fisher commentary request, and the special's availability.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts read listener mail from Amy J. Moffatt about the Voynich Manuscript podcast and then sign off with contact information and a plug for the website.
